Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About the Role & Team

As a Sensor Hardware Test intern, you'll work alongside our test engineering team to characterize and validate the sensors - cameras, lidar, and supporting hardware - that power Bedrock's autonomous excavators. You'll help build test fixtures, run structured lab test campaigns, and turn raw sensor data into clear conclusions that guide how we select and integrate hardware. You'll also get out to our field site to see how bench results hold up on a live construction machine. You’ll own a hands-on project involving sensor hardware testing end-to-end, and your results will directly shape what hardware ends up on the next generation of machines.

What You'll Do

- Build and iterate on test fixtures and benchtop setups - mechanical mounts, wiring harnesses, DAQ integration - used to characterize camera, lidar, and other sensor hardware

- Run structured sensor test campaigns in the lab, following defined test procedures and capturing repeatable, well-documented data

- Help safely deploy test setups and instrumentation out at our field site, and support live field test campaigns on active construction equipment

- Develop tools to automate data collection, process raw sensor logs, and summarize results against pass/fail criteria

- Help scope and select test equipment (light meters, targets, DAQ hardware, valves and actuators for environmental or fluid test rigs) for new test setups

- Support electrical and mechanical debugging of test hardware, including wiring, sensor interfacing, and basic CAD work for fixture design

- Document test methods, results, and findings, and present conclusions to the test engineering team to inform sensor selection and system design decisions

What We're Looking For

Required

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optics, Mechatronics, or a related field

- Hands-on experience building or testing hardware through coursework, personal projects, or a prior internship

- Working proficiency in Python for data processing, scripting, or automation

- Comfortable with basic lab equipment and electrical debugging (multimeters, oscilloscopes, DAQ systems)

- Comfortable working outdoors and around active construction equipment, and willing to spend time on-site at our field test location for deployment and field testing

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical work clearly for a team

Preferred

- Exposure to cameras, lidar, radar, or other sensing hardware through coursework, internship experience, or personal projects

- Experience with CAD tools for mechanical fixture design

- Familiarity with Git and working within a shared codebase

- Prior coursework, internship, or project experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or controls

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited.

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

BACKGROUND: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. At work in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities to provide humanitarian aid to those in need. The IRC in Atlanta office was established in 1979 and has resettled over 30,000 refugees from more than 65 countries into the Greater Atlanta area. Serving over 5,000 individuals annually, we provide integration support including casework, education, healthcare navigation, and school enrollment services.

SCOPE OF SUPPLY CHAIN INTERN WORK: Work with Operations team to provide supply chain and operational support within the IRC Georgia and Florida offices. Assist with inventory management, fleet management, operational tasks, administrative tasks, and various other related duties. Please note that all internship positions are unpaid.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

· Check-out IRC staff and clients completing “shopping” visits to Contributions-In-Kind (CIK) stock room

· Physical inventory counts

· Label and organize donated household items

· Assist with unloading and loading inbound and outbound donated household items for IRC donors and clients

· Data entry of inventory counts into Excel and other platforms

· Use of personal, insured vehicle or IRC vehicle to transport donated items externally as needed

· Conduct weekly vehicle inspections according to checklist

· Comply with all policies, procedures, and protocols

· Submit intern hours on volunteer dashboard

· Other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS:

- Attention to detail, critical thinking skills, time management skills, and ability to work independently and part of a team
- Able to communicate professionally with internal and external stakeholders
- Experience working with Microsoft Office applications
- Previous supply chain/inventory experience is a plus
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written

REQUIREMENTS:

- Must submit intern hours on volunteer portal.

- Must pass a background check.
- Commitment of 12 hours per week for a minimum of 3 consecutive months.
- Must be at least 18 years old.
- Must be authorized to work in the United States. Please note that we are unable to provide sponsorship for a US work authorization.

This will be an in-person role. This role will report to the Supply Chain Coordinator.

The internship will be filled on a rolling basis. We will continue to accept applications until December 11th, 2026, or until the position is filled, whichever occurs first. Internship will begin the week of January 11th, 2027.

Professional Standards: All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

Cookies: https://careers.rescue.org/us/en/cookiesettings

Customer Care Leadership Development Program - New Graduate

Most jobs ask you to figure out your future before your first day. This one doesn't.

The Customer Care Leadership Development Program is a launchpad to becoming an effective leader at Carvana. You'll start as a Customer Care Advocate at our Tempe headquarters, revolutionizing the car-buying journey by making the process of buying and/or selling a car simple, seamless, and unforgettable.

Then, through our Carvana University Training, you'll progress through our advocate milestones and into our Emerging Leaders Development Program. By your one-year anniversary, you could be a salaried Team Lead or take your talent across the business.

About the role

This is a full-time, hourly role with an assigned schedule (typically 38-45 hours per week), based in person at our Tempe headquarters. The role includes regular weekend and potential holiday shifts, along with overtime opportunities based on business needs.

In this role, you will:

- Create exceptional experiences by building genuine relationships with customers, guiding them through their car-buying or selling journey with empathy and expertise (via inbound and outbound calls).

- Adapt and thrive in a fast-paced environment where new products and innovations keep us ahead of the competition. Staying current with evolving technology and product updates is a core part of the day-to-day.

- Problem-solve with a purpose, using your critical thinking skills alongside AI technology to actively listen to customer needs and find effective solutions in real time.

- Drive efficiency and accuracy by reviewing and verifying sensitive customer documentation (via casework) with the swiftness of a ninja.

- Deliver high-quality interactions worthy of our moms. Our always-on AI coach supports every customer interaction with real-time feedback and coaching.

- Opportunity to move from an hourly role directly into a salary position after completing the Emerging Leaders Development Program through Carvana University Training.

- Other duties as assigned.

Learn it, earn it, lead it

Every step of the path is backed by our Carvana University Training, so you build your skills through mentorship and coursework, not guesswork. As a participant in our Customer Care Leadership Development Program participant, you'll get to:

- Become an expert first, learning how to deliver amazing customer experiences before you're asked to lead others.

- Progress through our Advocate milestones, with clear expectations and frequent pay increases as you hit your performance goals.

- Join the Emerging Leaders Development Program, where you'll develop the leadership skills and credentials that unlock career opportunities in driving fast-growth operations.

- Move into Operational Leadership or across the business.

Your growth path: from Advocate to leader in your first year

Our "Careers Not Jobs" philosophy is real: 80% of our leaders were promoted from within, and we can't wait to see where this opportunity takes you. The traditional path looks like this:

- Day 1: Advocate 1 ($20/hr). Learn our systems, products, and AI tools while building genuine relationships with customers.

- Month 4: Advocate 2 ($21/hr). Strengthen your expertise by taking on more challenging calls while continuing to deliver amazing customer experiences.

- Months 6-9 ($24/hr): Senior Advocate. Become a go-to expert on your team.

- Month 9 ($24/hr + 90 day Merit Eligibility): Emerging Leaders Development Program. Build the leadership skills and credentials to lead the Carvana way.

- Month 12: Ready to elevate. Step into a salaried role starting at $60k/yr as a Team Lead or take your skills across the business.

Who we're looking for

- You earned your Bachelor's degree in the last two years and have a passion for customer service.

- You want a program with a real finish line, one built to launch you into operational leadership or a career across the business.

- You're curious how a real company actually runs, end to end, not just the part in front of you.

- You're tech-savvy: you navigate multiple systems like a pro, learn new tools with ease, and troubleshoot effectively.

- You're resilient and think critically: you have a high capacity for learning, adapt quickly to rapid change, and make thoughtful, caring decisions that support customers throughout their car-buying journey.

- You enjoy serving customers over the phone and have strong attention to detail while handling casework.

- You can read, write, speak, and understand English.

Investing in you: benefits and perks

At Carvana, we know when our people thrive, we all win. Our Total Rewards package goes beyond the basics, designed to support your growth, your well-being, and your success every step of the way.

Financial well-being

- Tuition reimbursement for those pursuing a bachelor's degree and a student loan repayment program for those who already have one

- 401(k) retirement plan with Carvana matching contributions

- Opportunity for overtime based on business need

- Employee Stock Purchase Plan and Carvana Shares annual grant program, allowing you to become a Carvana shareholder

Health and wellness

- 100% company-paid healthcare premiums for comprehensive medical coverage

- Dental and vision benefits

- Wellness programs focused on supporting your mental, physical, and financial health

- Pet care savings program, because we know your furry friends are family too

Work-life balance

- Generous paid time off: 13 days in your first year, increasing to 20 days in year two and 25 days in year five and beyond

- 9 company-paid holidays, including your birthday

And more!
